# Public-effect first observations

19 informed original projects, 43 source/manifest files and policy/current predictions were frozen before any source check. All 38 fresh JSON checks use the same current normal CLI and explicitly selected kernel. Before/after hashes match for every command; all source hashes still match. No source or manifest repair was made.

Finite project checks: 9 accepted, 10 refused. Selected Raw checks: 8 accepted, 11 refused. The four policy-gap cases accept in both profiles: external public Observe identity called from public Unitary, missing effect on public quantum identity/H processing, missing effect on a closed public observation function, and missing effect on an external public quantum function.

Only the library body differs between external-identity-unitary and external-reset-unitary; the caller source and public Observe signature are byte-identical. Identity accepts and reset rejects with an Observe/Unitary effect error in both profiles. This is the unstable public abstraction boundary identified by #355. It does not mean that the reset body obtained a false pure label.

Nine direct/transitive hidden observation/reset/discard cases, each checked in both profiles, produce eighteen genuine effect refusals. Every message records inferred Observe exceeding the asserted Unitary or Isometry. External Observe identity, private inference, ordinary classical inference and the proposed precise same-module control accept in both profiles.

One initial prediction was wrong: external Observe reset accepts in finite checking but the selected Raw preparation refuses `unsupported: selected concrete preparation does not support std::observe::reset`. The first source, prediction, stderr/stdout and command are unchanged. This is a concrete-profile barrier, not evidence that #355 public abstraction is implemented. No translation was invented to remove that failure.

This is a current baseline preparation only. There is no implementation, post-change observation, execution, general semantic theorem, source/runtime preservation, physical/resource claim, or issue completion. The same-module precision case selects a candidate internal rule for explicit review; #355 requires that the external public contract remain separate. The runtime reports checker_identity as unpinned despite this observer recording unchanged executable hashes. Process attestation and complete native tracing are not supplied.

Original sources, first-sources.json, fresh observer source and all raw first records are inert evidence. Any later implementation comparison must be a separately authored observer and capture, never an overwrite or automatic replay of these historical commands.
